scenes.visual: COLOUR MAP for both films (16:9, dark navy background, flat cartoon style, no molecular structures): haploid n = GOLD, diploid 2n = TEAL, triploid 3n = CORAL. Meiosis is a round gate labelled '2n → n' (the meiosis gate): one TEAL 2n cell enters and four GOLD n cells leave; any fusion of nuclei is a round gate marked '+'; mitosis is a thin GREY looping 'copy' arrow that never changes a token's colour. Cells and nuclei are drawn as simple dots or rounded blocks with a small white label (n, 2n, 3n). Plants are simple flat cartoons. The life-cycle wheel is a big ring drawn clockwise; any diagram not computed from data carries a small corner label 'schematic'. Same colour map as the first film. Title card 'The Gametophyte Moves Inside' fades in over the GOLD and TEAL wheel from the first film, which slowly rotates.

scenes.tts: The first film drew one wheel, gold after meiosis and teal after fusion. Now, at the top of a pine there is no water film. So how does a sperm reach an egg?
scenes.visual: The wheel from the first film with its meiosis and + gates. It shrinks into the corner as a tall cartoon pine tree rises on a dry ridge. The words 'no water film' appear in white beside the crown. A white question mark sits between a small cone and a larger cone.
scenes.narration: The first film drew one wheel, gold after meiosis and teal after fusion. Now, at the top of a pine there is no water film. So how does a sperm reach an egg?

scenes.tts: The pine tree is the sporophyte, so it is teal. Its cones make two kinds of spores, so the gold arc splits in two.
scenes.visual: The whole tree fills TEAL, labelled 'sporophyte, 2n'. The corner wheel redraws: its GOLD arc splits into two parallel GOLD lanes, labelled 'male' and 'female', both leaving the meiosis gate and both meeting again at the + gate.
scenes.narration: The pine tree is the sporophyte, so it is teal. Its cones make two kinds of spores, so the gold arc splits in two.

scenes.tts: In small pollen cones, meiosis makes microspores. Each one becomes a pollen grain. A pollen grain is not a sperm. It is a male gametophyte of a few cells.
scenes.visual: Zoom into a small cluster of pollen cones. A meiosis gate releases tiny GOLD dots labelled 'microspores'. Each dot swells into a GOLD pollen grain; inside, a few small GOLD cells appear, labelled 'male gametophyte: a few cells'. A crossed-out label 'sperm' flashes and disappears.
scenes.narration: In small pollen cones, meiosis makes microspores. Each one becomes a pollen grain. A pollen grain is not a sperm. It is a male gametophyte of a few cells.

scenes.tts: In larger seed cones, meiosis inside an ovule gives four megaspores. Only one survives. It grows into the female gametophyte, which forms eggs.
scenes.visual: Zoom into a scale of a large seed cone, where a rounded TEAL ovule sits. Inside it a meiosis gate releases four GOLD dots in a row, labelled 'megaspores'. Three fade to grey and vanish; one stays and grows into a GOLD tissue mass labelled 'female gametophyte, n', with a GOLD egg inside it. The GOLD tissue stays wrapped in TEAL ovule tissue.
scenes.narration: In larger seed cones, meiosis inside an ovule gives four megaspores. Only one survives. It grows into the female gametophyte, which forms eggs.

scenes.tts: Wind carries pollen to the ovule. A pollen tube grows and delivers sperm to the egg, with no outside water. Both gametophytes are still here, just shrunk. The female one stays inside the ovule. The male one travels as pollen.
scenes.visual: Wind lines blow GOLD pollen grains to the ovule. One grain sends a GOLD tube growing through the TEAL tissue to the GOLD egg; a GOLD sperm moves down the tube. A grey label 'no outside water' with a crossed-out blue droplet. The corner wheel highlights both GOLD lanes, now drawn small: the female lane tucked inside a TEAL ovule outline, the male lane drawn as a pollen grain crossing to it from outside.
scenes.narration: Wind carries pollen to the ovule. A pollen tube grows and delivers sperm to the egg, with no outside water. Both gametophytes are still here, just shrunk. The female one stays inside the ovule. The male one travels as pollen.

scenes.tts: The egg is fertilized, and a seed forms. The seed's food store grew from that surviving megaspore. Gold or teal?
scenes.visual: The + gate fires inside the ovule. The ovule rounds into a seed shown cut open in white outline only, with three layers: a thin outer coat, a large middle food store, a small central embryo. The middle layer pulses with 'food store: ?'. GOLD and TEAL swatches hover beside it.
scenes.narration: The egg is fertilized, and a seed forms. The seed's food store grew from that surviving megaspore. Gold or teal?

scenes.visual: Hold the uncoloured cut seed. A thin timer bar shrinks across the bottom.

scenes.tts: Gold. The food store is the female gametophyte, so it is haploid. The seed coat comes from the parent tree, teal. The embryo is the new sporophyte, teal too. One seed holds three generations.
scenes.visual: The food store fills GOLD, labelled 'female gametophyte, n'. The outer coat fills TEAL, labelled 'parent sporophyte, 2n'. The embryo fills TEAL, labelled 'new sporophyte, 2n'. Three small arrows trace each layer back to a stage on the corner wheel. On-screen: 'one seed, three generations'.
scenes.narration: Gold. The food store is the female gametophyte, so it is haploid. The seed coat comes from the parent tree, teal. The embryo is the new sporophyte, teal too. One seed holds three generations.

scenes.tts: Flowering plants shrink the female gametophyte even further. Here too, the pollen grain is the male gametophyte. In Arabidopsis, the female one is the embryo sac, inside the ovule. Meiosis gives four megaspores, and three degenerate.
scenes.visual: Cross-fade from the pine to a small cartoon Arabidopsis plant with white flowers, filled TEAL, labelled 'Arabidopsis: sporophyte'. Zoom into a flower, then an ovule. A meiosis gate releases four GOLD dots; three fade away and one remains, labelled 'megaspore'.
scenes.narration: Flowering plants shrink the female gametophyte even further. Here too, the pollen grain is the male gametophyte. In Arabidopsis, the female one is the embryo sac, inside the ovule. Meiosis gives four megaspores, and three degenerate.

scenes.tts: The survivor's nucleus divides three times, without making new cells. Then walls form. Two cells matter here: the egg, and a large central cell holding two nuclei.
scenes.visual: Inside one GOLD oval, GOLD nucleus dots split: 1, then 2, then 4, then 8, the count shown on screen beside each step, no walls yet. Then thin white walls draw themselves. The egg at one end glows GOLD, labelled 'egg'. A large middle cell holding two GOLD nuclei glows, labelled 'central cell'. The camera frames only the egg end and the central cell; the far end of the sac stays out of frame, so no cell count is shown.
scenes.narration: The survivor's nucleus divides three times, without making new cells. Then walls form. Two cells matter here: the egg, and a large central cell holding two nuclei.

scenes.tts: Those two are the polar nuclei, and both are gold. In Arabidopsis they fuse before fertilization. Fusion adds, so the central cell is now two n.
scenes.caption: Those two are the polar nuclei, and both are gold. In Arabidopsis they fuse before fertilization. Fusion adds, so the central cell is now 2n.
scenes.visual: The two GOLD nuclei in the central cell are labelled 'polar nuclei'. They drift through a small + gate and merge into one TEAL nucleus. On screen: 'n + n = 2n'. The central cell outline turns TEAL.
scenes.narration: Those two are the polar nuclei, and both are gold. In Arabidopsis they fuse before fertilization. Fusion adds, so the central cell is now 2n.

scenes.tts: A pollen tube brings two sperm. One fuses with the egg, giving a teal zygote. The other fuses with the central cell.
scenes.visual: A GOLD pollen tube grows into the embryo sac and releases two GOLD sperm. Sperm one passes through a + gate with the egg: a TEAL dot labelled 'zygote, 2n'. Sperm two heads to the TEAL central cell and reaches a second + gate.
scenes.narration: A pollen tube brings two sperm. One fuses with the egg, giving a teal zygote. The other fuses with the central cell.

scenes.tts: Fusion adds again. The result is endosperm, a food tissue, and it carries three sets. That holds in Arabidopsis and most flowering plants, but not all.
scenes.visual: The second + gate fires: TEAL central nucleus plus GOLD sperm gives a CORAL nucleus. On screen: '2n + n = 3n'. The CORAL cell divides into a CORAL tissue labelled 'endosperm, 3n: a food tissue'. The greyed CORAL 3n in the legend lights up. A small footnote: 'Arabidopsis and most flowering plants, not all'.
scenes.narration: Fusion adds again. The result is endosperm, a food tissue, and it carries three sets. That holds in Arabidopsis and most flowering plants, but not all.

scenes.tts: Every label came from the same two gates. Meiosis halves the sets, and fusion adds them. Size and place changed, but meiosis still starts each gametophyte, and fertilization each sporophyte. Extra fusions add the endosperm. The female gametophyte now stays inside the ovule.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the corner wheel, now full size: TEAL sporophyte arc, a small female GOLD lane drawn inside a TEAL ovule outline, the male GOLD lane drawn as a pollen grain outside it, and a small CORAL branch off the female lane at a + gate for endosperm. Only the meiosis and + gates glow. The moss, fern, pine and flower icons sit around the wheel, each linked to it.
scenes.narration: Every label came from the same two gates. Meiosis halves the sets, and fusion adds them. Size and place changed, but meiosis still starts each gametophyte, and fertilization each sporophyte. Extra fusions add the endosperm. The female gametophyte now stays inside the ovule.

scenes.visual: End card: the hexagon mascot holds a TEAL seed cut open to show GOLD and TEAL layers. Line: 'Same two gates; the female gametophyte now stays inside the ovule.'
